content.title: Pistons playoff injury report: Cade Cunningham ‘getting close’ to 100%
content.text: PistonsDetroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham, right, looks to shoot against Orlando Magic guard Anthony Black, left, and forward Franz Wagner (22) during the second half of an NBA Cup basketball game Friday, Nov. 28, 2025, in Detroit. (AP Photo/Ryan Sun)APBy Jacob Richman | jrichman@mlive.comOne of the major benefits of locking up the No. 1 seed in the East early by the Detroit Pistons has been getting to rest up for the postseason.Detroit still had some work to do down the stretch securing its first 60-win season in 20 years and re-introducing Cade Cunningham and Isaiah Stewart to the rotation after extended absences. But getting to cycle their players and having nearly a week without a game has them in a great spot health-wise ahead of Sunday’s Game 1 against the Orlando Magic.The Pistons’ early injury report Saturday evening showed that, as it was completely clear for Detroit.Orlando’s lone player still uncertain to play is forward Jonathan Isaac, who is questionable due to a left knee sprain.Even though that’s great news for the Pistons’ availability, there’s still the key question of how ready Cunningham is to take on a typical or potentially expanded work load after missing 11 games due to a collapsed lung.It was a unique experience for Cunningham going through that rehab process and given how important it is to ramp back up cardio after such an injury, the Pistons took care with his final three appearances of the season.He played about 25 minutes per game, averaging 11.3 points on 44% shooting and 10.3 assists. While the amount of scoring production wasn’t quite there, Cunningham quickly made an impact again for Detroit.Following those games and a handful of practices with his team, Cunningham believes he’s nearing the quality he was playing at before the injury.“I’m getting close, man. I don’t think I’m back yet,” Cunningham told reporters Friday. “Obviously I still have some things that I’m still trying to get back to full speed and just get my rhythm and everything back. But I’m getting close. I’m just knocking a little bit more of the dust off every day.”The postseason often sees star players compete for longer stretches. That could still be the case for Cunningham with the Pistons as they get further into this opening series. Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff believes Cunningham is at 100%.However, with a deep roster ready to make an impact, the Pistons aren’t planning to minimize the contributions of their bench at this point.Pistons level playoff series with Magic behind explosive 2nd halfWhere to watch the Detroit Pistons vs. Orlando Magic Game 2 for free tonightDetroit Pistons odds: NBA playoff futures and betting odds to win the championship, Eastern Conference Finals and more in 2026Detroit Pistons fans can still score playoff tickets for tonight’s Game 2 for under $60Why didn’t Ausar Thompson play more in Game 1?
